walkthroughs.body_html:
Number — a core area of GCSE Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Number brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Number.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

options: π

mcqs.q: What is the reciprocal of the mixed number 2 1/3?
options: The object is moving backwards.
-2 1/3, because reciprocal means 'opposite'.
1/2 1/3, by flipping each part of the mixed number separately.
3/7 — first convert to the improper fraction 7/3, then flip it.

mcqs.q: On a distance-time graph, what does a horizontal line mean?
options: The object is moving backwards.
The object is moving at a constant speed.
Expressions are easier versions of equations.
The object is stationary — distance is not changing, so speed is zero.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between the expression 3x + 5 and the equation 3x + 5 = 11?
options: An expression has no equals sign and cannot be solved; an equation states two things are equal and can be solved for x.
Expressions are easier versions of equations.
-2 1/3, because reciprocal means 'opposite'.
Expressions and equations are the same — you can solve either one.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Prime number”?
options: A number that can be written as a fraction of two integers (e.g. 1/2, -3, 0.75).
Result of multiplying an integer by itself (1, 4, 9, 16, 25…).
A number that cannot be written as a fraction; its decimal goes on without repeating (e.g. √2, π).
Whole number greater than 1 with exactly two factors: 1 and itself.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Rational number”?
options: A whole number, positive, negative or zero (e.g. -3, 0, 17).
A number that can be written as a fraction of two integers (e.g. 1/2, -3, 0.75).
Result of multiplying an integer by itself three times (1, 8, 27, 64…).
Whole number greater than 1 with exactly two factors: 1 and itself.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Integer”?
options: Result of multiplying an integer by itself (1, 4, 9, 16, 25…).
A whole number, positive, negative or zero (e.g. -3, 0, 17).
Whole number greater than 1 with exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
Result of multiplying an integer by itself three times (1, 8, 27, 64…).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Cube number”?
options: A number that can be written as a fraction of two integers (e.g. 1/2, -3, 0.75).
Whole number greater than 1 with exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
Result of multiplying an integer by itself three times (1, 8, 27, 64…).
A whole number, positive, negative or zero (e.g. -3, 0, 17).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Square number”?
options: Result of multiplying an integer by itself three times (1, 8, 27, 64…).
A number that cannot be written as a fraction; its decimal goes on without repeating (e.g. √2, π).
A whole number, positive, negative or zero (e.g. -3, 0, 17).
Result of multiplying an integer by itself (1, 4, 9, 16, 25…).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Irrational number”?
options: A whole number, positive, negative or zero (e.g. -3, 0, 17).
A number that cannot be written as a fraction; its decimal goes on without repeating (e.g. √2, π).
A number that can be written as a fraction of two integers (e.g. 1/2, -3, 0.75).
Whole number greater than 1 with exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
